title: System for automatic storage and withdrawal of objects, and object transfer device used in the system

features.item: A housing with a grip portion designed as a hollow body for gripping
An electrically operated vacuum generating device in the housing
Exhaust air from the vacuum generating device guided through the hollow grip portion to an air outlet
A sound-damping device arranged in the grip portion
A suction plate with carrier plate and seal extending around the carrier plate
A grip unit with hollow grip portion, electrically operated vacuum generator, exhaust air routed through grip to outlet, and sound-damping in grip
Grip unit and suction plate combined in a vacuum handling apparatus
Grip portion at least partially lined with sound-damping material
Vacuum generating device arranged completely in a first housing portion
Sound-reducing device in the first housing portion or first housing portion lined with sound-reducing material
Grip portion elongated between first and second housing portions with air outlet on second housing portion
Air collection screw upstream of grip portion in first housing portion for collecting exhaust air
Bent or curved air baffles downstream of grip portion directing exhaust air to air outlet
Battery coupling point on second housing portion with air baffles directing exhaust air away from battery coupling point
Grip unit and suction plate releasably connected via a coupling device
Grip unit with suction opening fluidically connected to suction chamber delimited by suction plate

claims.note: This reference describes an object transfer device for storage and retrieval systems, not a grip unit for a vacuum hand-operated laying device.
This reference describes an object transfer device with a support structure and handling means, not a housing with a grip portion and an electrically operated vacuum generating device.
This reference does not describe a grip portion designed as a hollow body.
This reference does not describe exhaust air being guided through a grip portion to an air outlet.
This reference describes an object transfer device and system, not a grip unit for a vacuum hand-operated laying device, and does not mention any sound-damping device or grip portion.
This reference does not describe a grip portion lined with sound-damping material.
This reference does not describe a vacuum generating device or its arrangement within a housing portion.
This reference does not describe a sound-reducing device or lining in a housing portion.

This reference describes an object transfer device with housing areas and handling means, but it does not describe a grip unit with an elongated grip portion between first and second housing portions, nor an air outlet on a second housing portion.
This reference describes an object transfer device, but it does not describe an air collection device, an air collection screw, or the collection of exhaust air upstream of a grip portion.
This reference describes an object transfer device, but it does not describe air baffles, bent or curved, for guiding exhaust air emerging from a grip portion to an air outlet.

This reference describes an object transfer device, but it does not describe a battery coupling point for an electrical energy storage device or rechargeable battery on a housing, or air baffles for directing exhaust air away from such a point.
This reference does not discuss air baffles, exhaust air, or battery coupling points.
This reference describes an object transfer device and system, not a vacuum handling apparatus.
This reference does not describe a suction plate, carrier plate, or seal fastened to a carrier plate.
This reference does not describe a grip unit as defined in claim 1 of the subject invention.
The reference describes anchorage means for engaging containers, but does not disclose a grip unit and suction plate releasably connected via a coupling device.

claims.quote: A device according to claim 8 , characterised in that the gripping means comprise a suction cup member ( 74 ).
claims.note: The reference discloses gripping means comprising a suction cup member, which implies a suction opening and the ability to generate a vacuum. However, it does not explicitly state that the grip unit has a suction opening fluidically connected to a suction chamber delimited by a suction plate to generate a vacuum.

overall.why: This reference describes an object transfer device and system for storage and retrieval, which is a very broad area, but it does not disclose any of the specific features related to a vacuum handling apparatus with a grip portion, vacuum generation, or sound damping.
